experiment: ExpB — does the shipped DSA-native default ride the radix v_h jitter? (cold vs warm output/logprob parity across a radix cache hit)
envelope: TP8 / fp8_e4m3 / page64 / mem0.8 / max-running 64 / cuda-graph-max-bs 64 (expandable_segments NEVER set). DSA-native default (NO --enable-double-sparsity).
probe: OUTPUT/LOGPROB via standard /generate (return_logprob, top_logprobs_num=20). GREEDY temp0 top_k1. 16 decode steps. No new production code.

prompt.source: IDENTICAL deterministic text as the DS cold/warm probe (dec9_determinism q2_driver): '[i] The quick brown fox...' x316 + ' Summarize the passage above in one sentence.'

runs.v1_GRAPH_ON: DISCARDED for the cold/warm verdict: graph-on made even the radix-OFF fresh-vs-fresh control non-reproducible AND the warm send got cached_tokens=0 (radix miss). Re-ran EAGER.
runs.v2_EAGER_radix_miss: EAGER, but warm still cached_tokens=0 — traced to a PROBE BUG: logprob_start_len=0 forces full-prompt input logprobs which DISABLES radix prefix caching. Diagnostic (radixhit_diag) confirmed DSA-default radix DOES hit when logprob_start_len is omitted (short->64, medium->1024, 6090-tok->6080).
runs.v3_EAGER_radix_hit: FINAL. Probe fixed (omit logprob_start_len). EAGER. B1 warm got a REAL radix hit (cached_tokens=6080); B2 radix-OFF control.

control_is_NOT_bit_identical.finding: The radix-OFF control (two FRESH identical requests, EAGER, no cache hit at all) is NOT bit-reproducible: step-0 top-k logprobs differ by ~1.47-1.50 in BOTH the v2 and v3 boots, and in v3 the greedy continuation flips at step 9 just like B1. (In v2 the v2-control continuation happened to stay identical — the step-9 argmax sits on a near-tie that tiny run-to-run noise flips. step0_topk_max_dlp v2=1.499, v3=1.470.)
control_is_NOT_bit_identical.implication: Because the radix-OFF fresh-vs-fresh baseline ALREADY diverges by the same magnitude and at the same step as the radix-hit B1 cold-vs-warm, the probe CANNOT attribute B1's divergence specifically to the radix cache hit. The DSA-native GLM-5.1 decode is non-bit-reproducible run-to-run REGARDLESS of radix.

verdict.headline: PARTIAL / HONEST-NEGATIVE on the radix-specific claim.
verdict.cold_warm_bit_identity: The shipped DSA-native default does NOT meet a cold==warm bit-identity bar: B1 cold (fresh) vs warm (real radix hit, cached_tokens=6080) produce DIFFERENT step-0 logprobs (top-k |Δ| up to 2.19) and the greedy continuation diverges at step 9. So 'cold==warm bit-identity' is indeed a bar the shipped product does NOT meet.
verdict.but_not_radix_specific: However the spec's discriminating condition (B1 warm!=cold WHILE B2 fresh==fresh bit-identical) is NOT satisfied: B2 fresh-vs-fresh is ALSO non-identical (diverges at the same step 9, comparable |Δ|). The non-reproducibility is a general run-to-run property of the GLM-5.1 DSA decode (numeric jitter in the all-reduce/MoE/indexer path), present even with radix fully OFF. The radix hit does NOT add a distinguishable extra divergence above that baseline.
verdict.honest_conclusion: I CANNOT show that the DSA default specifically 'rides the radix v_h jitter', because the DSA default is not bit-reproducible even without radix. What is established: (1) the DSA-native radix cache DOES hit (cached_tokens 6080 on the identical 6090-token re-send), and (2) neither cold-vs-warm NOR fresh-vs-fresh is bit-identical at the OUTPUT/LOGPROB level for the shipped DSA default. The 'cold==warm bit-identity' criterion is stricter than the shipped product meets, but the gap is run-to-run numeric nondeterminism in general, not a radix-cache-specific effect isolable at the output level.

caveat: This OUTPUT-level probe cannot see DSA's internal indexer selection (not exposed by DS instruments). The DS-side dec9_determinism Q1 proved DS SELECTED-INDEX equality fresh-vs-fresh (integer top-k, a coarser quantity); raw output logprobs are a finer probe and jitter even when selected indices are stable. So 'DSA rides the radix v_h jitter at the selection level' is neither confirmed nor refuted here — only the OUTPUT/logprob level was observable, and at that level even fresh-vs-fresh is non-reproducible.
cleanup: v1, v2, v3 + diagnostic each torn down to ~0 MiB between boots; final nvidia-smi all 8 GPUs 0 MiB; no lingering sglang processes; expandable_segments never set; one TP=8 server at a time.
